Multispecies false-positive occupancy model

Source: R/fp_occu_ms.R
fp_occu_ms.Rd

Fits the false-positive occupancy model of fp_occu() to several species at once, with the coefficients of each species drawn from distributions of the community, so that rare species borrow strength from the others. This function is in development (see crywolf-api): its arguments, results and output names may change in a minor version. Besides print(), summary() and as_draws_df(), it works with fp_sites() (by site and species), fp_ppc(), simulate() and fp_richness(); the other methods of fp_occu() are not available.

Usage

fp_occu_ms(
  data,
  occ = ~1,
  det = ~1,
  fp = ~1,
  random_recorder = !is.null(data$recorder),
  ver = ~1,
  priors = fp_priors(),
  by_species = character(),
  random_fp = FALSE,
  fp_group = NULL,
  centered = FALSE,
  centered_occ = FALSE,
  chains = 4,
  parallel_chains = chains,
  threads_per_chain = "auto",
  iter_warmup = 1000,
  iter_sampling = 1000,
  adapt_delta = 0.95,
  seed = NULL,
  refresh = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_ms'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_ms'
summary(object, prob = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_ms'
as_draws_df(x, ...)

Arguments

data

An fp_data object with a species column; see the species argument of fp_data().

occ, det, fp, random_recorder, ver, priors

As in fp_occu(). The standard deviations among species have the half-Normal priors of fp_priors(species_sd = ); the community means have the priors of the intercepts, slopes and gap of fp_priors().

by_species

Terms that vary by species besides the intercepts of occ, det and the gap: any of "det" (the slopes of det), "fp" (the slopes of fp) and "ver" (the intercept of the verified method, so that the reviewer may miss some species more often than others). The default, character(), shares them among species. A term without slopes (for example "det" with det = ~ 1) adds nothing.

random_fp

Add a random effect on the logit of the false-positive rate for each site and species? See Details.

fp_group

Optional name of a column of the sites table that groups the sites; adds a random effect on the logit of the false-positive rate for each group and species. See Details.

centered

Use the centred parametrization of the detection intercepts, gaps, recorder effects and the terms of by_species? The model is the same. TRUE suits passive acoustic monitoring, with thousands of occasions per species: their posteriors are then so narrow that the default takes very small steps and reaches the maximum tree depth. Keep FALSE with few occasions per species or recorder.

centered_occ

Use the centred parametrization of the occupancy coefficients of the species? The model is the same. Their posteriors narrow with the number of sites, not of occasions: TRUE suits many sites (in simulations of 50 species at 100 sites, the default left the community occupancy intercept poorly mixed), and FALSE few sites, where the centred form samples worse.

chains, parallel_chains, threads_per_chain, iter_warmup, iter_sampling, adapt_delta, seed, refresh, ...

Passed to the sampler, as in fp_occu(). Runs of detections (markov) and site effects on true detection (random_det) are not available.

x, object

An fp_occu_ms object.

digits

Number of digits to print.

prob

Width of the equal-tailed credible interval.

Value

An object of class fp_occu_ms, a list with fit, draws (readable names: see Details), stan_data, formulas, design, data, by_species, random_fp, fp_group, random_recorder, priors, sampler, diagnostics and call.

summary() returns an object of class summary.fp_occu, as for fp_occu().

Details

Each species \(s\) has its own occupancy coefficients \(\beta_s = \mu_\beta + \sigma_\beta z_s\) (all the terms of occ, with \(z_s\) standard normal), its own true-detection intercept \(\alpha_s = \alpha + \sigma_\alpha z_s\), and its own gap between the true-detection and false-positive intercepts, \(g_s = \mu_g \exp(\sigma_g z_s)\), which keeps the false-positive rate of every species below its true-detection rate at the reference. By default the slopes of det, fp and ver, the intercept of the verified method and the recorder effect are shared by the species; by_species gives each species its own slopes of det or fp, or its own intercept of the verified method, drawn around the community value as the intercepts are (\(\alpha_{sk} = \alpha_k + \sigma_{\alpha k} z_{sk}\)). The false positives of a species are independent of those of the others: the classifier errs in labelling a species, not in confusing two species.

Two random effects let the false-positive rate vary beyond its covariates, on its logit, both with the half-Normal prior of fp_priors(fp_site_sd = ): fp_group names a column of the sites that groups them (for example the physical site, when each "site" of the data is a site in one month), and adds an effect for each group and species, \(v_{gs} \sim N(0, \sigma_v)\); random_fp = TRUE adds an effect for each site and species, \(t_{is} \sim N(0, \sigma_t)\). With sites that are site-months, fp_group lets the false-positive rate of a species differ among physical sites, and random_fp among months of the same site as well.

The species are those of the data (fp_data(species = )), and a species is never assumed to be absent from the list: there is no data augmentation for species never detected.

Output names. The community means have the names of fp_occu() (occ_*, det_*, fp_*, fp_gap, the median gap, and p11_ref, p10_ref at the community means); the standard deviations among species are sd_occ_*, sd_det_(Intercept) and sd_log_fp_gap; and the values of each species carry its name in brackets: occ_*[species], det_(Intercept)[species], fp_gap[species], p11_ref[species] and p10_ref[species]. With by_species, the slopes add sd_det_*, det_*[species], sd_fp_* and fp_*[species], and the verified method adds sd_verified_(Intercept), verified_(Intercept)[species] and p_verified[species]. The standard deviations of the random effects on the false-positive rate are sd_fp_group (fp_group) and sd_fp_site (random_fp).

See also

fp_data(), fp_occu(), simulate_fp_ms(), fp_richness()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# name every species to keep (`schema.json` lists them)
x <- fp_read_sheepdog("occupancy_export",
                      species = c("ela_bic", "lep_fus", "phy_cuv"))
d <- fp_draws_data(x, n_draws = 1)[[1]]
m <- fp_occu_ms(d, fp = ~ 1)
m
} # }
